title: CmdPal: Uninstall can leave commands from a stopped extension (EXT26.E2)

evidence: A test reproduced an empty removal notification after the provider had stopped and its registry entry was removed.
The report links WinRTExtensionService and CommandProviderWrapper construction/removal paths.
No assignee or matching issue-number PR was found in the focused search.
judgment.recommended_action: Use the targeted maintainer reproduction to validate the proposed mechanism before design approval; no upstream action has been taken.
judgment.rationale: The issue identifies an uninstall ordering defect and an isolated reproduction in which registry removal succeeds but the provider-removal notification is empty. Installed-host command removal still needs validation.

fix_assessment.rationale: No matching fix was found by focused issue-number search; treat the reported mechanism as a hypothesis and validate before implementation.

verification: With a test extension stopped before uninstall notification, verify its commands are removed without new remote calls.
Register a same-ID replacement before delayed removal and verify it remains intact.
Run focused CmdPal service/view-model tests and confirm installed-host uninstall removes visible commands.
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The uninstall path constructs a fresh CommandProviderWrapper after the extension has stopped; liveness/provider calls can fail, omitting removal after deleting the registry entry.
plan: Retain provider identity/lifetime before removing the registry entry; do not make remote provider calls to rediscover it.
Report removal from retained local state and identify the exact provider instance so delayed removal cannot delete a same-ID replacement.
Test stopped-extension uninstall and same-ID replacement; validate visible command removal in an installed host.

confidence.rationale: The empty notification is reproduced and source-linked; installed-host and same-ID lifetime behavior remain to be tested.
